ratings_why.fun: Choosing what to play last and where to seat it is a real decision every turn, and the growth goes from Courier and Red Sky early to the Warden's flood late, so the board keeps climbing.
ratings_why.distinct: Announced puts the tribe's payoff on any tribe's best unit, and out-of-turn Gusts that you have to sequence play unlike today's tribes. Extra attacks on their own are a familiar auto-battler idea.

verdict_why: Every tier does its job and every loop has a per-fight cap; more passes would change the flavour, not improve the climb.

points.text: The Warden's +20/+20 a fight per Announced unit, doubled by the Helm and again by Sir Vane, makes Tier 6 the whole game. A Tier 5 taste of it, such as a smaller cap, would smooth the climb from Tier 4 to 6.
Gust Page stops working once Bora or the Helm Gusts first. It could gain +1/+1 when it doesn't Gust, so it stays useful in the midgame.
The Bag-Bearer is thin for Tier 4: one Bag gives 4 stats and one Gust. Putting the Bag straight onto the Announced unit, or giving one each turn it stays, would bring it up to its tier.
Two Thunderheads (a second copy, or Sir Vane copying one) both 'attack after your other units'. A line saying reading order breaks the tie would settle it.
Tiers 1 to 3 have little permanent growth outside the Courier and Red Sky, and Bristle punishes early Gusts. One more early buffer would steady the opening.

standouts.why: Counting Thunder and keeping the forecast from setting him off early is a seating puzzle inside the tribe's own engine, and the payoff is loud.
A second Announced unit eases the play-order squeeze and doubles every Announced payoff; a clear Tier 4 multiplier.
Making the enemy's biggest units Gust into his thorns turns their strength against them, and it ties into Bog folk and the Windhover.

weakest.why: Low output for Tier 4, and nothing new happens after you play it.
About half a gold a turn is slow economy, and the Foul Gust only comes every other fight.
Only the first Gust Page fires, so it falls off quickly and copies don't add up.

flags.note: Permanent growth capped per fight but not per game; golden Warden plus the Helm plus Sir Vane can add 150+ stats a fight.
Copying a capstone from Tier 5, and golden Vane copying two, is the high roll most likely to run away.
Free Gusts plus +2/+2 per Gust kill, together with the Thunderhead's ten Gusts and Mistral's re-Gusts, stacks a lot of free value.
Shutting off every enemy Start of Combat effect may feel like a lock against Start of Combat builds, Gale mirrors included.
Attack order between two units that each 'attack after your other units' isn't stated.
